_comment: Symbol-size ratchet pins (#1155). MEASURED values, never round ceilings. Taken at the bench's own flags (Release = -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=c++23) on the toolchain named below; sizes are compiler-bound, so the gate refuses to compare across toolchains. Re-pin with: python3 bench/symbol_ratchet.py --build bench/build --pins bench/symbol_ratchet.json --emit

symbols.note: RE-PINNED 384 -> 368 (-16 B) by #1664 (config_t::kInstrumentCounters). The canonical-fallback arm's relaxed `fetch_add` on the node-wide `target_canonical_resolves` instrument is compiled out of the default (lean) build; nothing in the library read it — only the #830 ablation test and bench_target_binding, which opt in to the instrumented preset. The bound leg is untouched (it never counted). fan_out and every other pin are +0. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 427 -> 384 (-43 B) by RFC-0028 slice 9 (scatter-gather egress + ingress loan). This function's source is untouched: it is slice 7's inline-budget flip reversed, exactly. graph.cpp's TU gained the cold `value_t::make_loaned` / the loaned arm of `value_t::destroy` (both `[[gnu::noinline, gnu::cold]]`, pulled in through `value.hpp`), GCC 13.3 re-partitioned the unit's inline budget, and `count_store_drops` is an out-of-line CALL again instead of inlined here. Verified by call set: the slice-9 body calls {acl_allows, count_store_drops, deref_vertex_slot, find_ptr, store_value, value_t::release}, the base body the same set minus count_store_drops. The -43 B is that cold drop tally leaving; per-edge work is unchanged, fan_out and every other pin are +0. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 384 -> 427 (+43 B) by RFC-0028 slice 7 (one callback idiom, D10). No per-edge work was added: a HANDLER target is now handed the published block by reference (the adopting store_value overload calls the noinline handler_write directly, no try_rope clone), and with that clone path gone from graph.cpp GCC 13.3 re-partitions the TU's inline budget and inlines count_store_drops into this body instead of calling it out of line. The +43 B is that inlined drop tally (a cold, drops-nonzero path). The always-inline dispatch_edge body inside fan_out is unchanged (fan_out 1893 -> 1893, +0). Priced on bench_lean_value_path: the new local-handler row at K=32 falls ~1,760 -> ~1,190 ns (16 B), 1 block / 40 B per publish unchanged. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 555 -> 384 (-171 B; hot body 519 -> 384 B, 128 -> 99 instructions, and the 36 B `.cold` clone is gone) by RFC-0028 slice 4 (target adopt, D2). The target leg no longer clones the delivered value into a `rope_t` and hands it to `store_value(rope_t&&)`: it calls the new adopting overload `store_value(vertex_t*, const value_t&, ...)`, which takes one reference on the published block. Removed from this body: the `value_t::try_rope` call and its OUT_OF_MEMORY early return, the on-stack `rope_t` and its two `~rope_t` calls (hot + the unwind pad that was the whole `.cold` clone). The call set is otherwise identical (`deref_vertex_slot`, `find_ptr`, `acl_allows`, `store_value`, `count_store_drops`, `value_t::release`). The clone did not disappear for the two shapes that cannot adopt (a HANDLER target, a caller-owned `value_storage_t`): it moved INTO the adopting `store_value`, which is not pinned and not on the stored-target arm. `edge_view_t` is 48 B and `fan_out`'s instruction stream is identical modulo `.cold` addresses, so `dispatch_edge`'s always-inline per-edge body is unchanged. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 627 -> 555 (-72 B) by RFC-0028 slice 3 (`value_t` replaces the LKV wrapper). The delivery clone changed from `try_clone_rope(rope_t&, const rope_t&)` — `rope_t::concat` inlined as one `.isra` call — to `value_t::try_rope`, which is `[[gnu::noinline]]` for exactly this symbol: inlined, its reserve-then-append loop made the function 692 B (+101); out of line it is one call and the body loses the `shared_ptr` release of the returned `store_value` handle (`_Sp_counted_base::_M_release`) for a one-word `value_ref_t` decrement whose teardown arm is the cold `value_t::destroy`. `edge_view_t` is 48 B, `dispatch_edge` is +0. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 595 -> 627 (+32) by the admission seam: this leg's store failure is no longer always a resource event, so it reads the status instead of assuming one. The old code discarded the result and counted OUT_OF_MEMORY unconditionally; a target's admission filter can now refuse a delivery, which is a POLICY refusal and belongs in `denied` beside the fan-in ACL denial counted a few lines above. The +32 B is that one `expected` compare and its branch, and the attribution is DIRECT rather than inferred: reverting only this hunk in a clean tree restores 595 B exactly, with every other pin here unmoved. Priced as a correctness-of-attribution trade — a counter that reads a rejected value as an exhausted node is worse than 32 B on a leg that is already noinline and off the wide-fan-out arm. The #1448 record this note replaces stands: at 595 B that pin was flat while the instruction stream moved 138 -> 148, which is why the two `e.caller()` reads on this leg are still deliberately not hoisted.

symbols.band_note: DECLARED BAND (#1849), moved down by #1816. #1816 shrinks this symbol for real (1099 -> 987 -> 965: `remote_ptr_t::reset()` inlined, only the last holder's delete out of line), so the band is re-based on the new floor. The 16 B width is the same GCC per-TU inline-budget flip the #1849 band covered: 1115 -> 1099 by #1712, 1099 -> 1115 by #1713, re-pinned on rebases of #1831 (twice), #1765 and #1833, each with an identical call set. Inside 965..981 passes `in band`; anything outside still fails.
symbols.note: RE-PINNED 987 -> 965 (-22 B) by the #1816 perf fix (`remote_ptr_t::reset` always inlined, its `delete` moved to an out-of-line cold `free_record`). A SHRINK: the edge_view_t teardown in this body is now a null test and a decrement per handle, with no out-of-line `reset()` call. Priced on `bench_libtracer` (grid + fan), interleaved A/B against origin/main 0f3ed6fb, best of 7 rounds, pinned to one runner CPU (bench CPUs busy with the gate queue, so indicative): inproc 64 B / fan 1024 p50 8200 -> 7370 ns, 110 -> 133 M deliv/s; 1 KiB / fan 1024 8100 -> 7310 ns; 4 KiB / fan 1024 8130 -> 7680 ns; fan-remote ladder neutral. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1099 -> 987 (-112 B) by #1816. A SHRINK and NOT new work: `snapshot_edges` source is unchanged; the same graph.cpp inline-budget re-partition that moves `copy_published` (see its note). PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1115 -> 1099 (-16 B) by #1712 (per-vertex pending-mark hint). A SHRINK, and NOT new work: `snapshot_edges` source is unchanged; #1712 edits graph.cpp's `propagate_impl` / `mark_pending` / `clear_pending` and adds two private one-line flag helpers to `vertex_t`, which re-partitions the TU's inline budget — the same budget-sensitive flip the notes below record for this symbol. Pinned from the CI symbol-ratchet run (GCC 13.3). PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 955 -> 1115 (+160 B, 224 -> 252 instructions) by RFC-0028 slice 4. NOT new work: `snapshot_edges` does not touch a value, and its source is unchanged. It is the same INLINE-BUDGET FLIP slice 3 recorded below, one notch back the other way: graph.cpp's TU lost `try_clone_rope`, the rope clone and its unwind pad in `dispatch_edge_target` (-171 B), GCC re-partitioned the TU's unit-growth budget, and the one out-of-line `std::_Sp_counted_base::_M_release()` call this body made is now INLINED (the call count goes 1 -> 0 and `_M_release_last_use_cold` 1 -> 2 — the inlined copy's cold tail). The +160 B is exactly that inlined atomic decrement and its branch; every other call (`copy_published` x2, `segment_ptr_t::reset` x4, `operator delete` x4, the hazard `mutex::lock`) is unmoved. An inlined release trades a call for its body on a once-per-fan-out path (not per edge), priced on the interleaved A/B in the PR. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 843 -> 955 (+112 B, 199 -> 253 instructions) by RFC-0028 slice 3. NOT new work: `snapshot_edges` does not touch a value, a `value_ref_t` or the LKV slot, and its source is unchanged. It is the INLINE-BUDGET FLIP this file already documents for `fan_out` (#1461) and `copy_published` (#1442): graph.cpp's TU lost the `std::shared_ptr` control-block machinery and the `rope_t` clone paths, GCC's unit-growth budget re-partitioned, and the same call set (`copy_published` x2, `segment_ptr_t::reset` x4, `operator delete` x4, `_Sp_counted_base` x2, the hazard `mutex::lock`) now sits under two more `lock xadd` refcount legs inlined where a shared helper was, +18 `mov` / +6 `cmp` of the same sequences duplicated across the inline and overflow arms. The value it moved by is itself budget-sensitive: an earlier cut of the same change measured 1115 B here. Priced on the bench, interleaved A/B best of 3 rounds pinned to one core on a host at load avg 60-100: `bench_libtracer fan` (the snapshot_edges-dominated sweep) inproc fan 16/64/128/256/1024 is +24.9/+10.3/+16.5/+26.8/+5.6 % deliv/s with p50 -23/-19/-7/-6/-5 %, fan 8/32 -5.3/-1.3 % (inside the same-host A/A null, which spanned -9.7..+5.6 %). Neutral to favourable; the growth is not paid for in time. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 923 -> 843 (-80, 210 -> 199 instructions) by #1448. This is the -O3 WRAPPER, not the copy loop (see the `copy_published` note) — what it inlines is the entry `inline_buf.clear()` / `overflow.clear()` pair, which DESTROYS `edge_view_t`s, and those lost two `std::string` and two `view_t` members. The instruction histogram says exactly that: the inlined refcount-release legs collapse (`xchg` 6 -> 1, `lock` 5 -> 3) and the branches they were guarded by go with them (`je` 18 -> 12, `jmp` 10 -> 6), against two more `call`s where the remaining release is now outlined. A shrink, in the same direction and from the same cause as `copy_published`.

RE-PINNED 1871 -> 1860 (-11 B) by #1719 (config_t::kFaultInjection). A SHRINK: the bench build binds the lean default, so the `probe_fail_hook` load and branch on every nothrow growth and default-source draw compile out; this symbol's source is unchanged and the delta is the inlined `probe_hook_ok` check leaving its overflow-arm reserve. Re-pinned as the new floor. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1707 -> 1871 (+164 B, 399 -> 442 instructions) by RFC-0028 slice 3. Same INLINE-BUDGET FLIP as `snapshot_edges` above, same evidence: the source of `copy_published` and `copy_entry` is untouched and the call set is identical (`_Sp_counted_base` x2, `operator new`/`delete` x2, the length_error and catch legs) — the delta is +20 `mov`, +6 `movzbl`, +3 `pxor`/`xor`, one more `lock xadd`: the `edge_view_t` construct-and-move sequence emitted once per arm (inline buffer / reserved overflow) where the pinned build shared one copy. Per-edge work is unchanged: four words and two refcounts, no branch on the edge shape. Priced on the same `bench_libtracer fan` A/B as `snapshot_edges` (this symbol is its copy loop): neutral to favourable across the fan-out sweep. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 3554 -> 1707 (-1847 B, 761 -> 399 instructions) by #1448 — the change this pin was set to watch, arriving as a HALVING. `edge_view_t` stopped owning the cold half's bytes and started holding a `remote_ptr_t` share of it, so the per-entry copy is four words and two refcounts with no branch on the edge shape. What left the loop: the two `tr::detail::try_assign` probe-then-commit windows and their OOM unwind, the two `view_t` clone legs, and the whole per-edge `false` return path (`copy_published` no longer has a per-edge OOM tally — nothing on it can allocate). Instruction histogram: `mov` 301 -> 164, `call` 33 -> 12, `endbr64` 4 -> 2 (two fewer outlined helper entries). Priced on `bench_libtracer fan`, not argued from the disassembly. PREVIOUS NOTE, still the reason this symbol is pinned at all: ADDED by #1442. `snapshot_edges` was already pinned and stayed byte-identical (923 B, +0) across that change — but at -O3 it is only the wrapper: the pinned reader's ACTUAL copy loop is emitted out of line as `copy_published`, and it moved 4157 -> 3554 B (-603, 866 -> 761 instructions) with the pin set blind to it. `try_copy_published`'s source is untouched by #1442; the movement is an inlining-heuristic shuffle triggered by `pub_edge_t::remote` changing type from `std::unique_ptr<pub_remote_t>` to the intrusive `remote_ptr_t` (one `edge_view_t` move constructor outlined, and two `view_t::operator=` legs re-emitted as `segment_ptr_t::reset` calls). It is a SHRINK, and it was priced on the bench rather than argued from the disassembly: fanout-1 and the wide fan-out arms of bench_libtracer were within the same-window A/A null. Pinned here so the next such move is seen at review time instead of by hand.

RE-PINNED 1903 -> 1831 (-72 B) by ADR-0084 (remote AWAIT answered from a receiver-side waiter). An INLINE-BUDGET flip of graph.cpp back to the pre-#1844 size, not a change on the fan-out path: fan_out's source is untouched; graph.cpp gains the cold waiter arm/disarm/fire members, and GCC 13.3 re-partitions the TU. Not priced on the bench by this re-pin; the perf gate prices the PR. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1831 -> 1903 (+72 B) by #1844 (delete the owning decode, #1829), measured after its rebase onto 215c3e9c (#1851's graph_fields split). An INLINE-BUDGET flip of graph.cpp, not new per-edge work: fan_out's source is untouched; graph.cpp lost its owning-`tlv_t` readers (the subscriber parse and config reads now walk `tlv_node_t`), and GCC 13.3 re-partitioned the TU so one `std::_Sp_counted_base::_M_release()` call is now inlined (calls 3 -> 2, `_M_release_last_use_cold` 1 -> 2) with its indirect dispose/destroy pair duplicated at that site. The per-edge dispatch loop is unchanged and every other graph pin is +0 (graph_t::read and acl_allows are byte-identical to main). Priced on bench_libtracer inproc-fan, interleaved A/B against origin/main 215c3e9c, best of 6 rounds, one runner CPU (indicative): fan 1/8/128 flat (120/170/1000 -> 120/170/990 ns p50), fan 1024 7340 -> 7070 ns, fan 8192 57049 -> 55640 ns. Neutral to favourable. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1829 -> 1831 (+2 B) by the #1816 perf fix. Its two per-edge snapshot teardown loops called `remote_ptr_t::reset()` out of line on every edge, BEFORE #1816 too (8 % of a fan-1024 profile on main); that reset is now inlined there as a null test and a decrement, and the record's free is a cold call. Net +2 B, and the per-edge call is gone. Priced on `bench_libtracer` (grid + fan), interleaved A/B against origin/main 0f3ed6fb, best of 7 rounds, pinned to one runner CPU (bench CPUs busy with the gate queue, so indicative): inproc 64 B / fan 1024 p50 8200 -> 7370 ns, 110 -> 133 M deliv/s; 1 KiB / fan 1024 8100 -> 7310 ns; 4 KiB / fan 1024 8130 -> 7680 ns; fan-remote ladder neutral. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1893 -> 1829 (-64 B) by #1816. A SHRINK and NOT new work: `fan_out` source is unchanged; the same graph.cpp inline-budget re-partition that moves `copy_published` (see its note). PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1573 -> 1893 (+320 B) by #1461/#1462 (the receiver-owned STREAM ring). The growth is an INLINE-BUDGET FLIP, not new work on the fan-out path, and it is attributed at instruction level: `std::vector<edge_view_t>::~vector()` — one `call` in the pinned build — is now emitted INLINE at fan_out's cleanup paths, which is the whole delta (5 `operator delete` + 4 `segment_ptr_t::reset()` call sites where there were 1 and 2). It sits on the WIDE-fan-out teardown, below the no-subscriber gate and outside the per-edge loop; the per-edge dispatch body is unchanged, still one indirect callback call plus the two noinline legs, and `dispatch_edge_target` / `dispatch_edge_remote` / `snapshot_edges` / `copy_published` are all byte-identical (+0). The trigger is graph.cpp's own inline estimate moving: `store_value` gained the receiver-ring admission branch and `vertex_t::store` lost its STREAM fork, which re-partitioned the TU's budget — the same class of flip #1250 documents, in the other direction. PRICED ON THE BENCH before landing, as this gate's message demands: `inproc` 64 B / fan 1024 — the fan_out-dominated gated point — best of 3 rounds, interleaved A/B on one host under load avg ~22-39, is 7840 ns p50 against the pinned build's 8100 ns (-3.2%) and 126380 deliv/s against 122303 (+3.3%). Neutral to favourable, so the larger encoding is not paid for in time. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1613 -> 1573 (-40 B, 364 -> 361 instructions) by #1448. `fan_out` owns the `edge_snapshot_t` stack buffer and the thread-local overflow vector, both of which are arrays of `edge_view_t` — 160 B -> 48 B — so its frame setup and the two `for (const edge_view_t& e : ...)` strides re-encode against smaller displacements and a smaller stack reservation. The per-edge `dispatch_edge` body is unchanged apart from the remote-leg gate becoming `has_remote_leg()`, which is the same one load and one branch it was as `link.empty()` for the in-process edge that dominates a fan-out. The two reclamation bindings are unaffected: this pin measures the DEFAULT build, as the note below insists. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 1474 -> 1613 (+139) by #894 (ADR-0080 reclaim_local). The ONLY pinned symbol this change moves — the other four are byte-identical — and the growth is fully attributed at instruction level: ONE `addl $1,%fs:` on entry, plus a 5-instruction exit epilogue emitted THREE times (the wide TLS-buffer path, the small/stack path, and the .cold unwind clone), plus `nop` re-padding and two cleanup-frame displacement changes that add no instruction. The per-edge dispatch loop body is byte-identical, so the cost is once per fan_out regardless of subscriber count, and the no-subscriber early return is untouched. Priced on the bench: `inproc-batch` fanout-1 (the batch-calibrated bare-notify case) 102 ns -> 102 ns p50, +0.00%, against a same-day A/A null of +/-0.8%. rv32 (-Os, GCC 15.2) is +24 B and +6 instructions on entry; `reclaim_strict` is +0 instructions here. NOT RE-PINNED by #1376 (reclaim_qsbr): this pin measures the DEFAULT binding, which stays at 1613 B (+0) — verified, and backed by object-file identity of graph.cpp.o's whole instruction stream against the pre-#1376 tree. For reference only and explicitly NOT gating: a build that BINDS reclaim_qsbr_t measures 1819 B here (+206), all of it the outermost-bracket announce, the exit epilogues' offline store and the drain early-out, emitted at each of fan_out's exit paths. The per-edge dispatch loop body is instruction-identical between the two bindings, and the announce sits below the no-subscriber gate, so neither a wide fan-out nor an unsubscribed publish pays for it. A QSBR size must never be pinned into this file: the gate runs the default build.

RE-PINNED 318 -> 350 (+32 B) by #1883 (a refused set_policy changes no member). The remote leg's source is untouched: graph.cpp's apply_policy now stages its blocks before applying, and GCC 13.3 re-partitions the TU so the refcount release in this function's cleanup path is inlined in place of the out-of-line call. Nothing on the delivery path changed; 350 B is a shape this leg has held before. Not priced on the bench by this re-pin; the perf gate prices the PR. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 350 -> 318 (-32 B) by #1798 (one subscriber door parse, admission_for tests its own flag). A SHRINK, and the remote leg's source is untouched: graph.cpp lost subscribe_wire's own record decode and the two callers' flag tests, and GCC 13.3 re-partitions the TU so segment_ptr_t::reset() is called out of line here again, the 318 B shape this leg has had before. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 318 -> 350 (+32 B) by RFC-0028 slice 7 (one callback idiom, D10). The remote leg's source is untouched; the same slice-7 TU re-partition (the per-handler rope clone leaving graph.cpp) lets GCC 13.3 inline segment_ptr_t::reset() here in place of the out-of-line call. The +32 B is that inlined release, which is the pin value this leg had before slice 3 (350). fan_out +0. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 350 -> 318 (-32 B) by RFC-0028 slice 3. The remote leg hands the sink `const value_t&` instead of `const rope_t&`; nothing is cloned on this leg either way, and the shrink is the `rope_t` argument plumbing that is no longer there. A SHRINK, re-pinned. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 318 -> 350 (+32) by the admission seam, and NOT by any edit to this function or to the leg that calls it — an inline-budget flip of the same genre as the 298 -> 318 re-pin before it. Bisected in a clean tree, one file and then one declaration at a time: applying `vertex.hpp` alone produces 350 B with `graph.cpp` pristine, and deleting just the two new `std::function` members from the PUBLIC `handlers_t` — the by-value registration struct, now 64 B wider — puts it back at 318 with everything else in place. So the cause is the width of a registration-time parameter type re-partitioning this TU's inline budget, not anything on the delivery path: nothing this function does changed, and the code around it was re-laid-out. The filters themselves are deliberately NOT on the vertex (see `graph_t::admissions_`), so no per-vertex memory probe moves.

RE-PINNED 546 -> 540 (-6 B) by #1778 (graph core onto the table source). The walk's start is now the tree root inside the one `roots_` block (`&roots_->root`, a load of the owner's pointer word) where it was `root_.get()` on a `unique_ptr`; the descent and `child_by_record` are unchanged, and every other pin is +0. A SHRINK, re-pinned as the new floor.

RE-PINNED 3735 -> 2004 (-1731 B) by #1794 (one FWD header parse per hop). A SHRINK from deleted work, not an inline-budget flip: the hop now makes ONE `rebuild_fwd_forward` call (was three: ctx, registry entry, ctx-less self-parse) and the rebuild reads the dst, op and fwd headers from the routing peek's `fwd_pre_t` instead of re-walking them; the strip walk and the self-parse arm are deleted. `rebuild_fwd_forward<rope_cursor_t>` 8831 -> 4933 B, `<span_cursor_t>` 4868 -> 3032 B, `reject_bus_name_hop` 1672 -> 1106 B; `read_fwd_header<span_cursor_t>` stays at 837 B (the #1859 guard holds). MCU flash: ESP-IDF v6.0 esp32c6 full_node at -Os (GCC 15.2), base 3f34fff7 vs this change: this symbol 746 -> 588 B, fwd_router.cpp.obj .text 64068 -> 59042 B (-5026), .flash.text 364308 -> 359298 B (-5010), full_node.bin 482496 -> 477360 B (-5136). Priced interleaved A/B in the #1794 PR body. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 2620 -> 3735 (+1115 B) by #1779 (net plane onto the allocation seam). An INLINE-BUDGET flip of fwd_router.cpp, not new work on the forward hop: this template's source is untouched. With the registry's names held as views, `entry_by_name` (the no-ctx fallback only) became small enough to inline whole (+559 B); it is now `[[gnu::cold, gnu::noinline]]` and called, and GCC 13.3 spent the freed budget inlining three `rope_cursor_t::for_each_span` calls (5 -> 2 out of line) and two of the three `rebuild_fwd_forward` calls (3 -> 1), with `block_array_t::grow` call sites 7 -> 10. Priced interleaved A/B, taskset one CPU (12), best of 5 rounds, origin/main 3b22ba63 vs the PR head (indicative, shared host): compact-forward 4 B-64 KiB p50 42.3-44.0 -> 42.4-43.8 ns (within +-0.8 % except one +3.4 % row at 64 KiB that a second run put at +0.2 %), compact-terminus above 1 KiB 4/16/64 KiB 167/249/818 -> 160/232/702 ns, fwd-demux fixed/scan 1-64 links -0.2 to +1.1 % p50 at 1-4 links, -0.5 to -2.5 % at 8-32 and +0.8 % at 64, fwd-demux-value 64 B-64 KiB -0.9 to +0.6 %, inproc 64 B/1 KiB/8 KiB unchanged. MCU flash, the cost this host pin proxies: ESP-IDF v6.0 esp32c6 full_node at -Os (GCC 15.2), base e2210abf vs this change: this symbol 744 -> 746 B (+2), fwd_router.cpp.obj .text 67572 -> 64044 B (-3528), whole image .flash.text 367276 -> 364894 B (-2382), full_node.bin 485376 -> 482928 B (-2448). This symbol runs only on the rope ingress path, which no bench row exercises directly. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 2939 -> 2620 (-319 B) by ADR-0084 (remote AWAIT answered from a receiver-side waiter). An INLINE-BUDGET flip of fwd_router.cpp, the #1829 flip reversed: this template's source is untouched; the TU gains the deferred-AWAIT plane (defer, fire, answer, cancel), and GCC 13.3 now calls the mount scan (`resolve_mount_deep<rope_cursor_t>`) out of line where #1829 had inlined it, while `fall_back_on_label_refusal` is inlined in its place. Call set otherwise identical. `read_fwd_header<span_cursor_t>` stays at 837 B (the #1859 guard holds). Not priced on the bench by this re-pin; the perf gate prices the PR. PREVIOUS NOTE: RE-PINNED 2620 -> 2939 (+319 B) by #1829 (delete the owning decode). NOT new work on the forward hop: the call set is identical except that `child_registry_t::for_each<entry_by_name>` (the mount-name scan) is now inlined, bringing a `memcmp` call. Deleting the owning-tlv_t code from fwd_router.cpp freed the file's inline budget and GCC 13.3 spent it here; 2939 B is the size this pin held before the #1503 residual. `read_fwd_header<span_cursor>` stays at 837 B and `parse_header` stays inlined (the #1859 guard holds). Priced interleaved A/B, taskset one runner CPU, best of 5 rounds, origin/main 92af940f vs da5ffb69: compact-forward 4/64/512 B p50 41.5/41.5/40.6 -> 40.9/40.7/40.9 ns, compact-terminus 126.9-130.8 -> 126.3-129.8 ns, fwd-demux fixed/scan 1/8/64 links flat to +5 % throughput, inproc 64 B / 1 KiB / 8 KiB p50 flat (120/140/190 ns), max RSS within run spread. This symbol runs only on the rope ingress path (scatter-gather transports), which no bench row exercises directly.
